counterfactual_rationale: ROCm SDPA integration produced hallucinated vision-language output. A ROCm hardware lane running the vision example or similar end-to-end multimodal inference would plausibly expose it.

The IMA comes from scheduler metadata not matching the FlashAttention call under full CUDA-graph cascade attention. A capture/replay integration test for that cascade configuration would plausibly trigger it.
The failure depends on NaN candidate logits and underfilled rows duplicating block IDs. Tests with NaN or sparse-logit distributions would plausibly reveal the selector bug.
An empty batch on an NPU rank creates a zero-sized Triton launch rejected by NPU parameter checks. A batch-size-zero edge test on the NPU backend would plausibly catch it.

The error appears during torch.compile on a B200 diffusion generation path using flash attention v4. A compiled end-to-end diffusion generation test on the affected hardware would plausibly expose it.

The fixed workspace was too small for 32K and heterogeneous prefill masks, causing CUDA runtime errors. Edge tests over long context lengths and mixed prefill batches would plausibly expose the capacity bug.
CPU MRoPE dispatch was accidentally deleted and restored. CPU backend CI that instantiates MRoPE would plausibly catch the missing dispatch.
The HTTP 500 occurs only when torch.compile traces the Qwen-image fused qk-norm-rope path. A compiled image-generation request test would plausibly exercise the symbolic-shape failure.

The regression is ROCm-specific precision loss from applying router weights after conversion to bf16/fp16. ROCm LoRA/MoE accuracy tests with realistic router weights would plausibly reveal the expert-routing change.

The failures occur on W4AFP8 with DeepEP: first a missing routed_scaling_factor and then mode-specific dtype handling. A W4AFP8 DeepEP normal/decode serving test would plausibly exercise both contracts.

The ROCm sparse-MLA path lacked metadata fields and mishandled a one-dimensional FP8 scale shape. ROCm CI with the Quark GLM-5.2 checkpoint or equivalent sparse-MLA metadata test would plausibly fail.
The NPU MoE dispatcher cached top_k as None and crashed during OLMoE startup. An NPU model-startup test for an MoE layer that omits top_k would plausibly expose it.

The record establishes a tuning script/config-function crash around per_channel_quant, not incorrect production kernel behavior in serving. It is treated as tooling/configuration rather than confirmed kernel correctness.

The crash occurs when EAGLE verify fallback reads max_context_len from a hybrid attention wrapper. A speculative-decoding integration test using that hybrid backend would plausibly hit the missing attribute.
The TPU/XLA backend OOM is caused by wrapping MoE as a custom op despite XLA functionalization. A TPU hardware CI job serving the Mixtral MoE configuration would plausibly expose it.
The record says the PDL routers read bias before waiting for the preceding producer. A static synchronization analysis of the router kernels could plausibly flag that read-before-wait pattern.

The ROCm HIP radix backend built compressed-KV metadata for a draft worker that lacked the required pools, causing graph-capture startup failure. ROCm CI covering DeepSeek-V4 speculative startup would plausibly expose it.

The failure emerges after repeated elastic expert-parallel scale cycles leak PyNCCL communicators and leave EPLB state wrong. A long-running elastic scale-up/down integration test would plausibly expose the OOM or availability failure.

The RL workflow releases GPU memory and then encounters FusedMoE expert-map tensors created too early on GPU. A colocated RL memory-release/update-weight integration test would plausibly catch this availability issue.

The assertions fail because dummy-format random FP4/NVFP4 scales violate assumptions meant for real weights. A load-format=dummy test with random scale values would plausibly expose the unnecessary assertions.

The bug is a global-vs-local expert count mismatch in the modelopt/trtllm FP4 MoE path. A configuration test varying TP and EP expert layouts would plausibly trigger the routing-logits dimension check.
The sparse CUTLASS kernels were not built for Hopper after a CMake change, causing a missing compiled-kernel error. Hopper CI that builds and serves a sparse model would plausibly catch this.
The ROCm Triton MXFP8 quantizer used the wrong block-scale exponent and drifted from the torch reference. A ROCm kernel-vs-reference quantization test over random blocks would plausibly fail.
Invalid -1 indices appear under tie-overflow and inf-score distributions in fused top-k, then FA3 dereferences them. Tests with degenerate ties and inf or large scores would plausibly expose it.

The W4A16 transpose decision was ambiguous when candidate qzeros shapes were identical for particular quantized models. Shape/config edge tests for GPTQ or AutoGPTQ metadata on ROCm would plausibly reveal it.
DP+EP execution passed combined hidden states into shared experts instead of the original hidden states. A full DeepSeek FP4 FlashInfer MoE serving test with DP+EP would plausibly catch it.

The backend selector chose TRITON_ATTN for encoder-only models even though it did not support encoder self-attention. A BERT or other encoder-only initialization test through the normal selector would plausibly fail.

The FlashInfer backend rejected FP8 models with k_scale and v_scale, preventing a supported FP8-KV model from launching. An end-to-end launch test for such a model with FlashInfer would plausibly expose it.

The trtllm_mha target-verify path silently used causal semantics for ENCODER_ONLY draft blocks, degrading draft behavior while final outputs stayed verified. A semantic comparison against bidirectional paged SDPA would plausibly catch it.
The diffusion FA4 custom op schema could not vary its return arity and failed on Blackwell. A torch.compile or warmup diffusion generation test on Blackwell would plausibly expose it.
